   - *Scenario:* Alice wants to transfer $100 from Account A to Account B. Two transactions might try to update Account A simultaneously.
   - *Pessimistic:* When Transaction 1 starts, it locks Account A. Transaction 2 waits. Transaction 1 completes, unlocks. Transaction 2 proceeds. Guarantees consistency but can cause bottlenecks/deadlocks.
   - *Optimistic:* Transaction 1 reads Account A balance ($500) and version/timestamp (v1). Transaction 2 reads same balance and v1. Both calculate new balance. Transaction 1 commits, checks if version is still v1. It is, so commit succeeds. Transaction 2 commits, checks version, sees it's now v2, fails/retries. Better for low contention, but requires retry logic.
